facts.condition: The entropic model surviving the coarse relaxation is incompatible with a posterior-consistency implication imposed by the binary channel transition law. Excluding it requires channel-specific distributional constraints or a direct code-level argument, rather than universal entropy geometry and copy constructions alone.

For any vanishing-error sequence of deterministic private-message block codes, uniformly sampling one channel use while retaining the complementary output history yields two message-dependence terms, conditioned respectively on the sampled outputs of the two receivers, whose difference approaches zero. The sampled input must remain the output of the original coordinate encoder rather than a history-selected replacement map.

A converse relaxation based only on the relevant entropy data, code-structure equalities, balanced message dependence, erasure-type conditional identities, scalar support constraints, universal finite-variable information inequalities, and finitely many ordinary copy extensions still admits a finite entropic model at the classical UV benchmark. That relaxation class therefore cannot certify a strictly stronger converse by itself.

assumptions: The accepted judgment is authoritative only for the manifested accepted claim identity and its stated mathematical scope.
These facts do not establish an exact sum-capacity, a new achievable scheme, or a tighter numerical capacity bound.
Vanishing-error code sequences have bounded rates, so their decoding-uncertainty defects vanish asymptotically.
